channel.title: AIBuilder Marketplace — new honest reviews
channel.description: Hand-researched, honest software reviews: real pricing, the honest knock, who should skip it. No hype, no invented numbers.

item.title: Piktochart Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: Piktochart: Free is $0, Pro is $15 per member per month billed monthly or $10 billed annually, Business is $20 monthly or $17 billed annually.

item.title: BidX Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: BidX: €295 for the default report, custom reports quote-only. The number that decides your bill is the one number the page does not print.

item.title: Pippit Review (2026): Free Tier, Then €9/mo
item.description: Pippit: On monthly billing Starter is €9/mo against a €15 list price. The meter is credits per attempt, not per usable result.

item.title: Salesflow Review (2026): Per-Seat Pricing & the Catch
item.description: Salesflow: Their own pricing page returns a 403 to us. The per-seat price falls steeply with team size — roughly $79 alone against $29.98 at fifty seats.

item.title: SimplyBook.me Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: SimplyBook.me — Free EUR 0: 50 bookings a month, 1 custom feature, 1 provider, no card needed.

item.title: Seel Review (2026): Real Pricing, Real Limits
item.description: Seel: Customers who add Worry-Free Purchase (formerly Return Assurance) pay roughly $2-$5, reported elsewhere as 3-5% of order value.

item.title: CrowdStrike Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: CrowdStrike: Falcon Go $7.99 per device per month, or $59.99 per device billed annually. Two numbers decide whether this is for you.

item.title: Jibble Review (2026): Free Tier & the Catch
item.description: Jibble: Their own claim on that page is a free forever plan with unlimited users, described as '100% free', with no credit card required.

item.title: MeetGeek Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: MeetGeek: Pro $9.99 per user per month with 20 hours of transcription. The meter is transcription hours and Pro gives you twenty a month.

item.title: Teikametrics Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: Teikametrics: $149 a month billed annually, or $179 billed monthly. Read the Advanced tier carefully, because it is not a subscription.

item.title: Thryv Review (2026): Annual Billing & the Real Cost
item.description: Thryv: Signature $340 a month, billed $4,068 annually. Before that call, list which of the bundled parts you would otherwise buy separately.

item.title: Customer.io Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: Customer.io: Essentials starts at $100 a month billed monthly, scaled by profiles. Credit where due — the overage rates are printed.

item.title: FreshBooks Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: FreshBooks: Lite $2.30 a month promotional, $23 regular, 5 billable clients. The meter is billable clients, not invoices or revenue: Lite stops at five.

item.title: Hubstaff Review (2026): Per-Seat Pricing & the Catch
item.description: Hubstaff: Their own worked example puts the Team plan at $10 per seat per month. The seat definition is the whole story and they state it plainly.

item.title: Postscript Review (2026): From $49/mo, and the Catch
item.description: Postscript: Starter is shown as $0 a month with a $49 monthly minimum spend, at $0.015 then $0.009 per SMS and $0.045 per MMS, plus carrier fees.

item.title: ServiceM8 Review (2026): Free Tier & the Catch
item.description: ServiceM8 — Free $0: 1 user, 30 jobs a month, 10 AI uses a day. The meter is jobs instead, and jobs are the thing you least control.

item.title: Sunsama Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: Sunsama: The plan card says $17 a month billed yearly, or $22 billed monthly, for the Pro plan, with unlimited usage and integrations.

item.title: Textline Review (2026): Real Pricing, Real Limits
item.description: Textline: Add-on message credits are $0.03 each, bought in advance. Two costs here are easy to miss and both are per month rather than one-off.

item.title: Xero Review (2026): Real Pricing, Real Limits
item.description: Xero: Early is $5 a month for the first three months and then $25. Read the second number, not the first.

item.title: Aura Review (2026): Real Pricing, Real Limits
item.description: Aura: Starter $37/month ($451 a year), Essential $77 ($931), Plus $157 ($1,891), Pro $237 ($2,851). Pass $15K and Starter stops being the plan you are on.

item.title: Employment Hero Review (2026): Per-Seat Pricing & the Catch
item.description: Employment Hero — Recruitment: a free ATS tier at $0, then $199, $359, $639 and $959 a month for 50, 100, 200 and 300 AI video interviews.

item.title: Filevine Review (2026): No Public Price — What We Found
item.description: Filevine — Their own wording: all packages are custom built for your team's needs. Nothing is priced, so everything is negotiable — which cuts both ways.

item.title: Gorgias Review (2026): Annual Billing & the Real Cost
item.description: Gorgias: Not priced per agent — their own line. Tickets beyond your allowance are $0.40 each, so a bad week costs money rather than attention.

item.title: Motive Review (2026): No Public Price — What We Found
item.description: Motive: The pricing page is a lead-capture form — a four-step email capture before any figure appears. A pricing page with a form where the prices should be.

item.title: TestGorilla Review (2026): Free Tier, Then $142/mo
item.description: TestGorilla: Free $0 with 10 credits a month, no card needed, including preset custom questions and 1 full-access seat.

item.title: Envoy Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: Envoy — Visitors: Basic free, Premium $362 per location per month, Enterprise quote-only. None of the prices on that page is a price you can budget from.

item.title: Freshworks Review (2026): Annual Billing & the Real Cost
item.description: Freshworks — On Freshdesk: Growth $19 per agent per month, Pro $55, Enterprise $89. Freshworks is not a product, it is five of them.

item.title: Webflow Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: Webflow: Starter free (2 staging sites, 1 full seat), Core $19/mo, Growth $49/mo. Three separate bills, and the pricing page shows them on separate tabs.

item.title: Airwallex Review (2026): What It Actually Costs
item.description: Airwallex: Local transfers to 120+ countries free; SWIFT transfers $15–$25 each. The honest headline here is that the FX markup is published at all.

item.title: Amplitude Review (2026): Free Tier & the Catch
item.description: Amplitude: Free $0 with 2 million events a month, permanently, no card required. Unlimited seats is genuinely unusual and worth the credit.
